identity.name: F-91W Digital
identity.one_liner: The 1989 Casio F-91W — the most-produced digital watch in history, the watch on the wrist of every kid who went through a school in the 1990s, and the watch that defined "the affordable digital" for forty years.

narrative.story: The F-91W was introduced in 1989 and has been in continuous production since. The watch is the most-cited affordable digital watch in the world, and the most-photographed — Presidents, soldiers, musicians, and schoolchildren have all worn it. The story: Casio released the F-91W as a $20 watch with a 7-year battery, an LED backlight, a daily alarm, an hourly chime, a stopwatch, and a calendar. The result is the watch that "anyone can afford" has meant for four decades. The 593 quartz module is the same one in the A158WA, A159W, and the W-59.
narrative.collector_notes: The F-91W has been on the wrists of Presidents (Obama wore one), soldiers (US military issued F-91W variants in the 2000s), and a former British PM. It is the most-cited watch in the "any watch is better than no watch" debate.
